There have been times in my life when I felt alone and distant from God—barely making it through each day until everything seemed to collapse around me. This song is for those moments when you feel you can’t stand any longer. Remember, our strength comes from Him, which is why a personal relationship with Jesus is so important.

There was a time when I chose my own path, and the farther I traveled, the further I strayed from God. Believing I could make it on my own was the greatest lie I told myself. Eventually, I fell. Although getting back up was difficult, I later realized that without that fall, I might never have sought Him. I never imagined I would one day be thankful for that season of my life.

Understanding forgiveness is essential to our spiritual lives. God makes it clear that we must forgive others as He has forgiven us. Unforgiveness can fill our hearts with anxiety, anger, pride, and selfishness. When we understand the purpose of forgiveness, we can embrace it more honestly. Forgiveness can free our own hearts from resentment even when reconciliation or healing of the relationship hasn't occurred.

You may feel that you’ve traveled too far down the wrong road or done things that can never be forgiven, but God is always ready to welcome you home. Like the prodigal son, we sometimes go our own way, believing we know best, only to realize how lost we have become. Open your heart and return to Him—you’ll discover that He has been waiting for you all along.

This song is deeply personal because I reached a point in my life when I had to release the regrets I had carried for so long. Psalm 103:12 (NIV) says, “As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.” When we take those words to heart, we begin to understand the depth of the Father’s forgiveness. Don’t let regret hold you captive. Choose to forgive yourself, and allow His peace, grace, and love to fill the space once occupied by all that pain and regret.

A couple of years ago on Easter, I heard a pastor describe how Jesus bore the sins of the world on the cross. I remember thinking, “He should not have had to do that—it should have been me.” I carried that thought with me and later turned it into this song.
In the Quiet, You're Still There

I wrote this song as a reminder that even when we don’t feel God’s presence, He is still with us. I don’t claim to understand His plan or how He uses life’s circumstances to draw us closer to Him. But I’ve learned that when I can’t feel Him in the storm, I may be the one who has drifted away. Sometimes the storm is exactly what I need to draw closer to God.

Sometimes I think we spend so much time worrying about what's wrong in our lives that we forget to celebrate what's eternally right. I've been saved by the grace of Jesus Christ! I didn't earn it by being good enough, and I could never deserve it through anything I've done. Salvation is God's gift, received through faith in Jesus Christ. Life isn't always fair or predictable, and I certainly don't get everything right, but God's faithfulness doesn't change with my circumstances. That's what inspired this song. It's an upbeat, joyful celebration of the grace that saved me, the mercy I never deserved, and the assurance that my salvation rests in Christ rather than my own accomplishments. Sometimes we need to set aside our worries, remember what Jesus has done for us, and simply celebrate the incredible gift of being saved by His grace.

I think sometimes we make prayer much more complicated than God ever intended it to be. We think we need to know the right words, sound a certain way, or somehow get ourselves into the right place before we can talk to Him. But I've come to understand that prayer is really just a conversation with God. He already knows what I'm afraid of. He knows my questions, my doubts, my disappointments, and the things I'm struggling to put into words. I don't have to hide any of that from Him, and I don't have to pretend my faith is stronger than it is. Sometimes the only prayer I may have is, “God, help me,” and I believe He hears that just as clearly as any prayer I could ever put together. That's what this song means to me. Wherever you are, whatever you're going through, and whatever words you have—or don't have—you can simply talk to Him.

This song was a long time coming. I grew up in a non-denominational church in the Midwest, and when I went to church, the sanctuary was a reverent place. When you presented yourself before God, you dressed accordingly. You were quiet. You were respectful. After all, you were in the house of the Lord.
That way of thinking became deeply ingrained in me, and it has taken me many years to understand the difference between showing reverence for God and believing that I somehow had to make myself presentable before I could come to Him.
I understand something very different today. God isn't concerned with how nice your clothes are, what kind of shoes you're wearing, whether your hair is combed, or whether you've managed to clean yourself up before coming to Him. God cares about your heart.
He doesn't ask you to get everything together first. He doesn't ask you to fix yourself before you approach Him. He simply wants you to come—with an open heart and a willingness to meet Him right where you are.

I have always thought one of the hardest parts of faith is learning to trust God when I don't understand what He is doing. I think most of us would like God to show us the whole plan—to tell us where we're going, how we're going to get there, and assure us that everything will work out the way we hope. But that's not really faith. I'm learning that trusting God doesn't mean I always feel confident or that I never have questions or fear. Sometimes trusting Him simply means taking the next step He's put in front of me, even when I can't see where the road leads. I don't have to understand everything God is doing to believe that He knows where He's taking me. I don't need to see the entire journey. I just need enough faith to put tomorrow in His hands and follow Him one step at a time.

This song is really about looking back over my life and realizing that even during the times when I couldn't see God, He was there. There were times I worried about tomorrow, times I tried to handle everything myself, and times when I probably wondered where God was in all of it. But the older I get, the more I can look back and see His hand in places where I didn't recognize it at the time. I've also come to appreciate something I probably took for granted when I was younger—every morning I open my eyes is a gift from God and another opportunity to become more of the man He wants me to be. Yesterday doesn't have to define today. I can get up, thank God for another breath, and keep moving forward knowing I don't have to walk the road alone. God was there through everything that brought me to this moment, He's here with me today, and I trust that He'll be there for every step still ahead.

“Faith Changes Everything” is more than the name of this song—it is the message at the heart of this ministry. I've learned that having faith in Jesus Christ doesn't mean every problem disappears or that I suddenly get everything right. It means I no longer have to face life the same way. His grace meets me in my failures, His Word gives me direction, and His promises give me hope when I can't see what lies ahead. The change isn't something I can accomplish through determination alone; it begins with what Christ has done for me and continues as He works in my life. This song is a declaration that no matter where we've been, what we've done, or how far we've wandered, we can come to Jesus Christ and be made new. Our circumstances may not change overnight, but through Him, our lives can be transformed. That's why I believe faith changes everything.
